definition: March of the Machines: Why the New Race of Robots Will Rule the World (1997, hardcover), published in paperback as March of the Machines: The Breakthrough in Artificial Intelligence (2004), is a book by Kevin Warwick.
details: It presents an overview of robotics and artificial intelligence (AI), often focusing on anecdotes of Warwick's own work, and then imagines future scenarios. In particular, Warwick finds it likely that such AIs will become smart enough to replace humans, and humans may be unable to stop them.

explainer.lead: March of the Machines is a 1997 book by Kevin Warwick, published in paperback in 2004 as March of the Machines: The Breakthrough in Artificial Intelligence. It matters as a widely cited statement of the view that AI could surpass and replace humans.

tiers.eli5: It is a book that tours today's robots and AI, then imagines a future where the machines outgrow us.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers encounter it as background in debates about AI risk and robot capability. The pitfall is treating its scenarios as predictions rather than speculation.
